# package candb

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canbus/candb"
```

Package candb is the format-independent model of a CAN message database and its signal codec.

DBC files (package dbc) and KCD files (package kcd) are parsed into a [Database](#type-database); the code generator (package codegen) and the dynamic codec of this package work on it, so every input format shares one runtime.

Raw signal values are exact: they are carried as 64-bit integers (the field's bit pattern, and its sign-extended value for signed signals) and never pass through floating point. Physical values are computed from them (raw × factor + offset) as float64.

A database describes messages and signals. It is not a protocol, and a message identifier names a message, not a device.

```go
	ErrRange          = errors.New("candb: value out of range")
	ErrMissingSignal  = errors.New("candb: signal value missing")
	ErrInactiveSignal = errors.New("candb: signal not present for this multiplexer value")
	ErrLayout         = errors.New("candb: invalid signal layout")

```


#### func PhysText

```go
func PhysText(s string) Input
```

PhysText is a physical value given as decimal text (a JSON number, a command-line argument). For an integer signal with factor 1 and offset 0, an integer text is the raw value exactly, without passing through float64, so 64-bit values keep every bit (as cantools' identity conversion and canmatrix's decimal arithmetic do). Otherwise it is the same as [Phys](#func-phys) of the parsed number.

#### func (Message) Decode

#### func (Message) Encode

```go
func (m *Message) Encode(values map[string]Input) ([]byte, error)
```

Encode encodes a message strictly: every signal the payload carries must be given and physical values must lie within their range.

#### func (Message) EncodeWith

```go
func (m *Message) EncodeWith(values map[string]Input, opts EncodeOptions) ([]byte, error)
```

EncodeWith encodes a message. The payload has Length bytes (for CAN FD messages rounded up to a CAN FD length) with unused bits 0. Values for unknown signals, or for multiplexed signals the multiplexer values do not select, are errors.

### type Signal

```go
type Signal struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
	// StartBit is the DBC start bit: the least significant bit for
	// little-endian signals, the most significant bit (in Intel bit
	// numbering) for big-endian signals.
	StartBit  int       `json:"startBit"`
	Length    int       `json:"length"` // bits, 1..64
	ByteOrder ByteOrder `json:"byteOrder"`
	Signed    bool      `json:"signed,omitempty"`
	ValueType ValueType `json:"valueType"`
	Factor    float64   `json:"factor"`
	Offset    float64   `json:"offset"`
	// Minimum and Maximum are the physical range; both 0 means none.
	Minimum   float64            `json:"minimum"`
	Maximum   float64            `json:"maximum"`
	Unit      string             `json:"unit,omitempty"`
	Receivers []string           `json:"receivers,omitempty"`
	Values    []ValueDescription `json:"values,omitempty"`
	Comment   string             `json:"comment,omitempty"`
	// Initial is the raw initial value (DBC attribute GenSigStartValue),
	// if known.
	Initial *int64 `json:"initial,omitempty"`

	// IsMultiplexer marks a multiplexer switch: its value selects which
	// multiplexed signals the payload carries.
	IsMultiplexer bool `json:"isMultiplexer,omitempty"`
	// Multiplexer names the switch this signal depends on ("" if it is
	// always present), and MuxValues the switch values for which it is
	// present. A switch may itself be multiplexed (extended
	// multiplexing).
	Multiplexer string     `json:"multiplexer,omitempty"`
	MuxValues   []MuxRange `json:"muxValues,omitempty"`

	Attributes []Attribute `json:"attributes,omitempty"`
}
```

### type Value

```go
type Value struct {
	// Raw is the field's bit pattern, zero-extended. For floating-point
	// signals it is the IEEE 754 bit pattern.
	Raw uint64 `json:"raw,string"`
	// Signed is Raw sign-extended for signed integer signals; for

	Signed int64 `json:"signed,string"`
	// Physical is the scaled value: Signed (or Raw, or the float) ×

	Label string `json:"label,omitempty"`
}
```
